title: Count Number of Substrings
problemStatement: Count substrings containing exactly k distinct characters.
intuition: Counting "exactly k" directly is awkward, but "at most k" is a clean sliding window. exactly(k) = atMost(k) - atMost(k-1).

approaches.title: Optimal: two at-most-K windows
approaches.idea: Each window is O(n); the subtraction gives the exact count.
approaches.whyWorks: Every window ending at right contributes right - left + 1 valid substrings.

commonMistakes: Trying to maintain "exactly k" in a single window
Deleting zero-count keys is required for len(freq) to be correct
patternRecognition: "Exactly K" -> atMost(K) - atMost(K-1); memorise this identity
interviewInsight: The at-most identity converts a whole class of hard counting problems into easy windows.
